summary: An audit citation that is EXEMPT from the digest check is still required to EXIST, which makes the exempt path permanently undeletable. The obvious migration for rogue3#53 - move all 96 entries out of the shared scripts/audit-binding-exceptions.json into the new per-cycle directory and delete the old file - would have broken four already-merged audits that cite that path, because FeedbackReportTool.resolveEvidencePath checks existence before digestExemption is consulted. The migration was written, then reverted in favour of keeping the file as a frozen archive.
evidence: file:.agents/skills/fs-gg-feedback-report/scripts/FeedbackReportTool.fs (digestExemption exempts the digest only; the existence check is upstream of it);command:python3 scripts/check-audit-bindings.py --json reports 4 notBoundCitations onto file:scripts/audit-binding-exceptions.json from feedback/audits/2026-08-02-Rogue3-7, -8, -11 and -17.audit.json;file:.agents/skills/fs-gg-feedback-report/SKILL.md (the locator still has to resolve inside the workspace and the file still has to exist - only the digest is unbindable)
cost: One written-then-reverted migration of a 774-line ledger, and a design decision reversed mid-cycle.
owner: FS-GG fs-gg-feedback-report - the exempt-but-must-exist rule turns every exempt path into a permanent repository fixture; a path whose digest is unbindable arguably should not be required to exist either.

summary: Changing one kit file needs three separate manual steps and only the first is discoverable. Editing .agents/skills/fs-gg-feedback-report/SKILL.md required (a) copying it to the .claude/skills mirror, (b) hand-editing the same sha256 in BOTH .agents/skills/skill-manifest.json and .claude/skills/skill-manifest.json, and (c) re-running ./fake.sh build -t KitPins because scripts/kit-pins.json pins the manifest. TemplateDrift names the drift precisely and names no command that fixes it; KitPins deliberately only pins what the manifest does not name, so it cannot repair a manifest digest.
evidence: command:./fake.sh build -t TemplateDrift reported 3 violation(s) naming .agents/skills/skill-manifest.json, .claude/skills/skill-manifest.json and the mirror for one SKILL.md edit, with no remedy command in the message;command:./fake.sh build -t KitPins pinned 63 kit file(s) and did not clear the manifest drift;file:build.fsx (KitPins pins only the complement the generated manifest does not name)
cost: Two TemplateDrift runs and a hand-edited digest in two files before the gate went green.
owner: EHotwagner/rogue3 build.fsx - TemplateDrift should name the repin command for a manifest-pinned file, or KitPins should be able to repin a deliberate manifest edit.

summary: A coordination acceptance criterion of the form two concurrent workers must not collide is provable cheaply and reproducibly in a throwaway git repository containing only the tool under test. Two branches from one base, each editing a different audit-bound file and running the remedy, then merged: pre-fix at 715bef9 the merge exits 1 with scripts/audit-binding-exceptions.json conflicted and the checker then exits 2 on the unreadable ledger; post-fix the merge exits 0 with no conflicted paths and the checker exits 0. The same harness run with both workers editing the SAME bound file shows the source file conflicting - correctly - while the ledger does not, and either resolution is green with no further remedy run.
evidence: command:a two-branch git harness over scripts/check-audit-bindings.py printed A touched [scripts/audit-binding-exceptions.json src/X.fs] and B touched [scripts/audit-binding-exceptions.json src/Y.fs], merge exit 1, conflicted paths [scripts/audit-binding-exceptions.json], post-merge check exit 2 at 715bef9;command:the same harness on the candidate printed A touched [scripts/audit-binding-exceptions/item-a.json src/X.fs], B touched [scripts/audit-binding-exceptions/item-b.json src/Y.fs], merge exit 0, conflicted paths [], post-merge check exit 0;command:the same-file variant printed conflicted paths [src/X.fs] only, and check exit 0 after resolving to either side without a further --grandfather run
owner: FS-GG intra-repo-parallel-work - a collision claim is testable rather than negotiable, and this shape of harness is worth naming in the skill.

summary: The 72 pre-existing cases in check-audit-bindings.py --selftest carried a structural rewrite of the very thing they test - one shared ledger file became the union of a directory of files - with only mechanical call-site edits and exactly one substantive failure, which was a wrong assertion in a NEW case rather than a regression. A gate whose self-test is in the same file as the gate, seeded over throwaway trees, is cheap enough to keep exhaustive: the suite went from 72 to 110 checks and still runs in well under a second, so it can be re-run after every edit rather than at the end.
evidence: command:python3 scripts/check-audit-bindings.py --selftest exits 0 with 72 ok lines at 715bef9 and 110 ok lines on the candidate;file:scripts/check-audit-bindings.py (selftest_per_cycle seeds one temporary tree per claim so an unrelated leftover violation cannot decide a verdict)
owner: FS-GG - the in-file self-test over throwaway trees is the reason a load-bearing gate could be restructured at all; it is worth stating as doctrine rather than leaving as this file's habit.
